# `csharp_space_after_unary_operator`

Space after unary minus/plus, logical not, and the unsafe pointer prefix operators. Not bitwise complement or prefix increment/decrement.

## Values

| Value | Notes |
|---|---|
| `true` |  |
| `false` |  |

**Default:** `false`

## Conformance

Curb's output is not always a fixed point of the tool(s) below for this key — see [conformance divergences](../../design-principles/conformance-divergences.md) for the full registry.

- **dotnet-format-whitespace**: csharp_space_after_unary_operator is a ReSharper generalized key (space_after_unary_operator) dotnet format does not recognise at all. Measured: dotnet format whitespace always normalises `- x`/`+ x`/`! x` back to `-x`/`+x`/`!x` regardless of any .editorconfig setting, since it has its own fixed, unconfigurable opinion here. Setting the key to true is a permanent, structural divergence from dotnet format for any file containing a unary expression — there is no shape Curb could pick that satisfies both dotnet format's fixed opinion and the key's own request at once. (`SpacingTests.Unary_minus_plus_and_not_take_a_space_when_asked`)
- **dotnet-format-whitespace**: Same permanent divergence as SpacingTests.Unary_minus_plus_and_not_take_a_space_when_asked, exercised for the two unsafe pointer prefix operators (pointer indirection `*p`, address-of `&x`) rather than unary minus/plus/not — dotnet format normalises `* p`/`& x` back to `*p`/`&x` just as unconditionally. (`SpacingTests.The_unsafe_pointer_prefix_operators_take_a_space_too`)
- **ide0055**: Same permanent divergence as the dotnet-format-whitespace entry above (a ReSharper-only key dotnet format has no concept of, so it always normalises the space back out), now confirmed under a real `dotnet build -p:EnforceCodeStyleInBuild=true` as well as the `dotnet format whitespace` CLI. (`SpacingTests.Unary_minus_plus_and_not_take_a_space_when_asked`)

### `csharp_space_after_unary_operator = true`

```ini
csharp_space_after_unary_operator = true
```

::::{tab-set}

:::{tab-item} Before
```csharp
namespace N;

public class Widget
{
    public int Negate(int x)
    {
        int a = -x;
        bool b = !(x > 0);
        int c = ~x;
        return a + c;
    }
}
```
:::

:::{tab-item} After
```csharp
namespace N;

public class Widget
{
    public int Negate(int x)
    {
        int a = - x;
        bool b = ! (x > 0);
        int c = ~x;
        return a + c;
    }
}
```
:::

::::
